</div>

Google reCAPTCHA is a powerful library that provides easy integration of Google reCAPTCHA into your React applications. Built with **TypeScript-first** approach, **SSR compatibility**, and **tree-shaking optimization** - everything you need to protect your forms and applications from spam and abuse.

## Supported reCAPTCHA Versions

- **V3** - Invisible protection that returns a risk score (0.0-1.0) for each request
- **V2 Invisible** - Background analysis without user interaction
- **V2 Checkbox** - Interactive "I'm not a robot" checkbox with optional challenges
- **Enterprise mode** - support [enterprise](https://cloud.google.com/recaptcha/docs/overview)

## Documentation

Visit https://siberiacancode.github.io/google-recaptcha/docs/react to view the full documentation.

## Packages

- [core](https://github.com/siberiacancode/google-recaptcha/tree/main/packages/core)
- [react](https://github.com/siberiacancode/google-recaptcha/tree/main/packages/react)
- [vue](https://github.com/siberiacancode/google-recaptcha/tree/main/packages/vue)
- [docs](https://github.com/siberiacancode/google-recaptcha/tree/main/packages/docs)

# explicit.mdx

Source: https://github.com/siberiacancode/google-recaptcha/blob/main/packages/docs/content/docs/core/guides/explicit.mdx

title: Explicit
description: Configure explicit rendering options for reCAPTCHA

## What is explicit rendering?

Explicit rendering gives you full control over how and where the reCAPTCHA widget is rendered. Instead of automatic rendering, you can specify exactly where and when the widget should appear.

## Basic Configuration

### v2 Checkbox

For v2 checkbox, you need to specify a container element where the widget will be rendered:

```ts
import { injectGoogleReCaptchaScript } from '@google-recaptcha/core';

const container = document.createElement('div');
container.id = 'recaptcha-container';
document.body.appendChild(container);

injectGoogleReCaptchaScript({
  render: 'explicit',
  container: 'recaptcha-container',
  onload: () => console.log('onload')
});
```

### v3 and v2 Invisible

For v3 and v2 invisible, you can control badge placement:

```ts
import { injectGoogleReCaptchaScript } from '@google-recaptcha/core';

injectGoogleReCaptchaScript({
  render: 'explicit',
  badge: 'inline',
  container: 'badge-container',
  onload: () => console.log('onload')
});
```

---

# hide-badge.mdx

Source: https://github.com/siberiacancode/google-recaptcha/blob/main/packages/docs/content/docs/core/guides/hide-badge.mdx

title: Hide badge
description: Learn how to hide the reCAPTCHA badge while complying with Google's terms of service

Sometimes you may want to hide the reCAPTCHA badge to implement your own privacy policy and terms of service display. This is a common requirement for applications that need to maintain a specific design aesthetic or want to present their privacy information in a more integrated way.

Google officially allows hiding the badge, but with an important requirement: you must include the reCAPTCHA branding and privacy policy text in your application's privacy policy or terms of service. This ensures users are still informed about the use of reCAPTCHA while maintaining your desired design.

## Official solution

The official way to hide the badge is through CSS. Google provides a specific class that you can target to hide the badge while maintaining compliance with their terms of service. Here's how to implement it:

```css
.grecaptcha-badge {
  display: none !important;
}
```

You can add this CSS to your global styles or component-specific styles.

## Using the helper function

For convenience, we provide a helper function `hideGoogleReCaptchaBadge` and [`generateGoogleReCaptchaHiddenBadgeStyles`](../references/generateGoogleReCaptchaHiddenBadgeStyles.mdx) that handles the badge hiding for you.

---

# theme.mdx

Source: https://github.com/siberiacancode/google-recaptcha/blob/main/packages/docs/content/docs/core/guides/theme.mdx

title: Theme
description: Learn how to customize the appearance of reCAPTCHA widgets

The Google reCAPTCHA provides two themes: "light" and "dark". When using the core package, you can configure the theme when injecting the script.

## Basic Theme Configuration

```ts
import { injectGoogleReCaptchaScript } from '@google-recaptcha/core';

injectGoogleReCaptchaScript({
  render: 'explicit',
  theme: 'dark', // or 'light'
  onload: () => console.log('onload')
});
```

## Badge Customization

For v2 invisible and v3, you can customize the badge position:

```ts
import { injectGoogleReCaptchaScript } from '@google-recaptcha/core';

injectGoogleReCaptchaScript({
  render: 'explicit',
  badge: 'bottomright', // or 'bottomleft', 'inline'
  onload: () => console.log('onload')
});
```

---

# index.mdx

Source: https://github.com/siberiacancode/google-recaptcha/blob/main/packages/docs/content/docs/core/index.mdx

title: Installation
description: Install and setup the core package for Google reCAPTCHA integration

The Core package provides fundamental utilities and types for Google reCAPTCHA integration. It serves as the foundation for both React and Vue implementations, offering a set of helper functions for script management, badge control, and type definitions.

## Installation

Install the Core package using your preferred package manager:

```package-install
npm install @google-recaptcha/core
```

## Features

- **Script Management**: Functions for loading, checking, and removing reCAPTCHA scripts
- **Badge Control**: Utilities for managing the reCAPTCHA badge visibility
- **Type Definitions**: Comprehensive TypeScript definitions for reCAPTCHA integration
- **Enterprise Support**: Built-in support for Google reCAPTCHA Enterprise
- **Framework Agnostic**: Can be used with any JavaScript framework

## Basic Usage

Here's a simple example of using the core package to load reCAPTCHA:

```ts
import { checkGoogleReCaptchaInjected, injectGoogleReCaptchaScript } from '@google-recaptcha/core';

if (checkGoogleReCaptchaInjected()) return;

injectGoogleReCaptchaScript({
  render: 'explicit',
  onload: () => console.log('reCAPTCHA loaded'),
  siteKey: 'your_site_key'
});
```

---

# checkGoogleReCaptchaInjected.mdx

Source: https://github.com/siberiacancode/google-recaptcha/blob/main/packages/docs/content/docs/core/references/checkGoogleReCaptchaInjected.mdx

title: checkGoogleReCaptchaInjected
description: Checks if Google reCAPTCHA script is already injected in the document

## Import

```ts
import { checkGoogleReCaptchaInjected } from '@google-recaptcha/core';
```

## Usage

```ts
checkGoogleReCaptchaInjected();
```

## Return

Returns `true` if the reCAPTCHA script is already injected, `false` otherwise.

## Examples

### Basic

```ts
if (checkGoogleReCaptchaInjected()) {
  console.log('Script already loaded');
}
```

### With Script Loading

```ts
if (!checkGoogleReCaptchaInjected()) {
  injectGoogleReCaptchaScript({
    render: 'explicit',
    onload: () => console.log('Script loaded')
  });
}
```

### With Cleanup

```ts
if (checkGoogleReCaptchaInjected()) {
  removeGoogleReCaptchaScript();
}
```

## Details

### Script Detection

Checks for:

- Script tags with reCAPTCHA source
- Excludes gstatic resources
- Both standard and enterprise versions

### Performance

- Synchronous operation
- DOM query based
- No network requests

## See Also

- [`injectGoogleReCaptchaScript`](./injectGoogleReCaptchaScript)
- [`removeGoogleReCaptchaScript`](./removeGoogleReCaptchaScript)

---

# generateGoogleReCaptchaHiddenBadgeStyles.mdx

Source: https://github.com/siberiacancode/google-recaptcha/blob/main/packages/docs/content/docs/core/references/generateGoogleReCaptchaHiddenBadgeStyles.mdx

title: generateGoogleReCaptchaHiddenBadgeStyles
description: Utility function for generating CSS styles to hide the Google reCAPTCHA badge

```ts
const styles = generateGoogleReCaptchaHiddenBadgeStyles();
```

## Return

Returns a string containing CSS styles that hide the Google reCAPTCHA badge.

<Callout>
  This utility is useful when you want to hide the reCAPTCHA badge while still complying with
  Google's terms of service. Make sure to include a visible reCAPTCHA badge or a text notice about
  reCAPTCHA usage on your page.
</Callout>

---

# generateGoogleReCaptchaScriptSrc.mdx

Source: https://github.com/siberiacancode/google-recaptcha/blob/main/packages/docs/content/docs/core/references/generateGoogleReCaptchaScriptSrc.mdx

title: generateGoogleReCaptchaScriptSrc
description: Utility function for generating Google reCAPTCHA script source URL

```ts
const scriptSrc = generateGoogleReCaptchaScriptSrc({
  host,
  isEnterprise,
  render,
  hl,
  badge
});
```

## Parameters

| Parameter      | Type                                        | Required | Default        | Description                                        |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------- | -------- | -------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `host`         | `string`                                    | -        | `'google.com'` | The host for the script source URL                 |
| `isEnterprise` | `boolean`                                   | -        | `false`        | Whether to use the enterprise version of reCAPTCHA |
| `render`       | `string`                                    | Yes      | -              | The render parameter for the script source URL     |
| `hl`           | `string`                                    | -        | -              | The language code for the reCAPTCHA widget         |
| `badge`        | `'bottomright' \| 'bottomleft' \| 'inline'` | -        | -              | The position of the reCAPTCHA badge                |

## Return

Returns a string containing the complete URL for the Google reCAPTCHA script.

# injectGoogleReCaptchaScript.mdx

Source: https://github.com/siberiacancode/google-recaptcha/blob/main/packages/docs/content/docs/core/references/injectGoogleReCaptchaScript.mdx

title: injectGoogleReCaptchaScript
description: Injects the Google reCAPTCHA script into the document

```ts
injectGoogleReCaptchaScript({
  badge,
  hl,
  host,
  isEnterprise,
  render,
  onload
});
```

### Parameters

The function accepts a configuration object with the following properties:

| Name           | Type                                        | Required | Default        | Description                  |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------- | -------- | -------------- | ---------------------------- |
| `badge`        | `'bottomright' \| 'bottomleft' \| 'inline'` | Yes      | -              | Badge position               |
| `hl`           | `string`                                    | No       | -              | Language code                |
| `host`         | `'google.com' \| 'recaptcha.net'`           | No       | `'google.com'` | Script host                  |
| `isEnterprise` | `boolean`                                   | No       | `false`        | Use enterprise version       |
| `render`       | `string`                                    | Yes      | -              | Rendering mode for reCAPTCHA |
| `onload`       | `() => void`                                | Yes      | -              | Callback when script loads   |

import { PackageIcon } from 'lucide-react';
import { ReactIcon, VueIcon } from '@/app/(components)/icons';

Google reCAPTCHA is a security service that protects your website from spam and abuse. This package provides a simple and efficient way to integrate Google reCAPTCHA into your applications, supporting all major frameworks and versions.

## Supported reCAPTCHA Versions

- **V3** - Invisible protection that returns a risk score (0.0-1.0) for each request
- **V2 Invisible** - Background analysis without user interaction
- **V2 Checkbox** - Interactive "I'm not a robot" checkbox with optional challenges
- **Enterprise mode** - support [enterprise](https://cloud.google.com/recaptcha/docs/overview)

## Framework support

# core.mdx

Source: https://github.com/siberiacancode/google-recaptcha/blob/main/packages/docs/content/docs/framework/packages/core.mdx

title: Core
description: Core utilities and types for Google reCAPTCHA integration

The Core package provides low-level utilities and types for integrating Google reCAPTCHA into your applications. It serves as the foundation for both React and Vue implementations, offering direct control over script lifecycle, badge management, and container handling.

## Installation

Install the Core package using your preferred package manager:

```package-install
npm install @google-recaptcha/core
```

## Basic Usage

The core package can be used directly to manage reCAPTCHA integration:

```ts
import { injectGoogleReCaptchaScript, checkGoogleReCaptchaInjected } from '@google-recaptcha/core';

injectGoogleReCaptchaScript({
  render: 'explicit',
  siteKey: 'your_site_key'
});

grecaptcha.ready(function () {
  grecaptcha.execute('reCAPTCHA_site_key', { action: 'submit' }).then((token) => {
    // ...
  });
});
```

## Enterprise Mode

Google reCAPTCHA Enterprise provides enhanced security features and analytics:

```ts
import { injectGoogleReCaptchaScript } from '@google-recaptcha/core';

injectGoogleReCaptchaScript({
  render: 'explicit',
  siteKey: 'your_enterprise_site_key',
  isEnterprise: true
});
```

---

# react.mdx

Source: https://github.com/siberiacancode/google-recaptcha/blob/main/packages/docs/content/docs/framework/packages/react.mdx

title: React
description: React integration for Google reCAPTCHA with hooks and components

The React package provides a comprehensive solution for integrating Google reCAPTCHA into React applications. Built specifically for React, it offers hooks, components, and providers that seamlessly integrate with your React workflow while supporting all reCAPTCHA versions including v3, v2-invisible, and v2-checkbox.

## Installation

Install the React package using your preferred package manager:

```package-install
npm install @google-recaptcha/react
```

## Provider Setup

All reCAPTCHA functionality requires wrapping your application with the `GoogleReCaptchaProvider`. This provider manages the reCAPTCHA script loading and provides context to child components.

```tsx
import { GoogleReCaptchaProvider } from '@google-recaptcha/react';

export const App = () => (
  <GoogleReCaptchaProvider type='v3 | v2-checkbox | v2-invisible' siteKey='your_site_key'>
    ...
  </GoogleReCaptchaProvider>
);
```

### V3

[Google ReCaptcha v3](https://developers.google.com/recaptcha/docs/v3) returns a score for each request without user friction. The score is based on interactions with your site and enables you to take an appropriate action for your site.

```tsx
import { useGoogleReCaptcha } from '@google-recaptcha/react';

const App = () => {
  const googleReCaptcha = useGoogleReCaptcha();

  const onVerify = async () => {
    if (!googleReCaptcha.executeV3) {
      console.log('Execute recaptcha not available');
      return;
    }

    // [!code word:executeV3]
    const token = await googleReCaptcha.executeV3('action');
    ...
  };

  return <button onClick={onVerify}>verify</button>;
};
```

### V2 invisible

[Google ReCaptcha v2 invisible](https://developers.google.com/recaptcha/docs/display) does not require users to solve any puzzles or enter any codes. Instead, it runs in the background and analyzes user behavior on the web page to determine if they are genuine users or potential bots.

```tsx
import { useGoogleReCaptcha } from '@google-recaptcha/react';

const App = () => {
  const googleReCaptcha = useGoogleReCaptcha();

  const onVerify = async () => {
    if (!googleReCaptcha.executeV2Invisible) {
      console.log('Execute recaptcha not available');
      return;
    }

    // [!code word:executeV2Invisible]
    const token = await googleReCaptcha.executeV2Invisible();
    ...
  };

  return <button onClick={onVerify}>verify</button>;
};
```

### V2 checkbox

When a user interacts with the [Google ReCaptcha v2 checkbox](https://developers.google.com/recaptcha/docs/display), advanced algorithms analyze their behavior to distinguish between humans and bots. If the system suspects suspicious activity, additional challenges may be presented, such as image selections or puzzle-solving tasks.

```tsx
import { GoogleReCaptchaCheckbox } from '@google-recaptcha/react';

const App = () => <GoogleReCaptchaCheckbox onChange={(token) => console.log(token)} />;
```

## Enterprise Mode

Google reCAPTCHA Enterprise provides enhanced security features, advanced analytics, and better customization options for businesses. It offers improved bot detection, detailed risk analysis, and enterprise-grade support.

```tsx
// [!code word:isEnterprise]
<GoogleReCaptchaProvider type='v3' siteKey='your_enterprise_site_key' isEnterprise>
  <App />
</GoogleReCaptchaProvider>
```

Enterprise mode supports some actions for better risk assessment and provides detailed analytics on user interactions.

```ts
const googleReCaptcha = useGoogleReCaptcha();

const onClick = async () => {
  // [!code word:'action']
  const token = await googleReCaptcha.executeV3('action');
  ...
};
```

---

# vue.mdx

Source: https://github.com/siberiacancode/google-recaptcha/blob/main/packages/docs/content/docs/framework/packages/vue.mdx

title: Vue
description: Vue integration for Google reCAPTCHA with composables and components

The Vue package provides a comprehensive solution for integrating Google reCAPTCHA into Vue applications. Built specifically for Vue 3, it offers composables, components, and providers that seamlessly integrate with the Vue Composition API while supporting all reCAPTCHA versions including v3, v2-invisible, and v2-checkbox.

## Installation

Install the Vue package using your preferred package manager:

```package-install
npm install @google-recaptcha/vue
```

## Provider Setup

Vue reCAPTCHA can be integrated in three different ways depending on your needs and application structure: **Plugin**, **Provider Component**, **Composable**

```ts tab="Plugin" title="main.ts"
import { createApp } from 'vue';
import { googleReCaptcha } from '@google-recaptcha/vue';

import App from './App.vue';

const app = createApp(App);

app.use(googleReCaptcha, {
  type: 'v3',
  siteKey: 'your_site_key'
});
app.mount('#app');
```

```vue tab="Provider Component"
<template>
  <GoogleReCaptchaProvider type="v3" site-key="your_site_key">
    <slot />
  </GoogleReCaptchaProvider>
</template>

<script setup>
import { GoogleReCaptchaProvider } from '@google-recaptcha/vue';
</script>
```

```vue tab="Composable"
<script setup>
import { useGoogleReCaptchaProvider } from '@google-recaptcha/vue';

useGoogleReCaptchaProvider({
  type: 'v3',
  siteKey: 'your_site_key'
});
</script>
```

## Usage Examples

### V3

[Google ReCaptcha v3](https://developers.google.com/recaptcha/docs/v3) returns a score for each request without user friction. The score is based on interactions with your site and enables you to take an appropriate action for your site.

```vue tab="Composable"
<script setup>
import { useGoogleReCaptcha } from '@google-recaptcha/vue';

const googleReCaptcha = useGoogleReCaptcha();

const onVerify = async () => {
  if (!googleReCaptcha.executeV3) {
    console.log('Execute recaptcha not available');
    return;
  }

  // [!code word:executeV3]
  const token = await googleReCaptcha.executeV3('action');
  ...
};
</script>

<template>
  <button @click="onVerify">Verify</button>
</template>
```

```vue tab="Component"
<script setup>
import { GoogleReCaptchaV3 } from '@google-recaptcha/vue';

const token = ref('');
</script>

<template>
  <GoogleReCaptchaV3 v-model="token">
    <button>Verify</button>
  </GoogleReCaptchaV3>
</template>
```

### V2 invisible

[Google ReCaptcha v2 invisible](https://developers.google.com/recaptcha/docs/display) does not require users to solve any puzzles or enter any codes. Instead, it runs in the background and analyzes user behavior on the web page to determine if they are genuine users or potential bots.

```vue
<script setup>
import { useGoogleReCaptcha } from '@google-recaptcha/vue';

const googleReCaptcha = useGoogleReCaptcha();

const onVerify = async () => {
  if (!googleReCaptcha.executeV2Invisible) {
    console.log('Execute recaptcha not available');
    return;
  }

  // [!code word:executeV2Invisible()]
  const token = await googleReCaptcha.executeV2Invisible();
  ...
};
</script>

<template>
  <button @click="onVerify">Verify</button>
</template>
```

### V2 checkbox

When a user interacts with the [Google ReCaptcha v2 checkbox](https://developers.google.com/recaptcha/docs/display), advanced algorithms analyze their behavior to distinguish between humans and bots. If the system suspects suspicious activity, additional challenges may be presented, such as image selections or puzzle-solving tasks.

```vue
<script setup>
import { GoogleReCaptchaCheckbox } from '@google-recaptcha/vue';

const onChange = (token) => console.log(token);
</script>

<template>
  <GoogleReCaptchaCheckbox @change="onChange" />
</template>
```

## Enterprise Mode

Google reCAPTCHA Enterprise provides enhanced security features, advanced analytics, and better customization options for businesses. It offers improved bot detection, detailed risk analysis, and enterprise-grade support.

```vue
<script setup>
import { GoogleReCaptchaProvider } from '@google-recaptcha/vue';
</script>

<template>
  <!-- [!code word:is-enterprise] -->
  <GoogleReCaptchaProvider type="v3" site-key="your_enterprise_site_key" is-enterprise>
    ...
  </GoogleReCaptchaProvider>
</template>
```

Enterprise mode supports some actions for better risk assessment and provides detailed analytics on user interactions.

```vue
<script setup>
import { useGoogleReCaptcha } from '@google-recaptcha/vue';

const googleReCaptcha = useGoogleReCaptcha();

  const onClick = async () => {
    // [!code word:'action']
    const token = await googleReCaptcha.executeV3('action');
    ...
  };
</script>
```

# explicit.mdx

Source: https://github.com/siberiacancode/google-recaptcha/blob/main/packages/docs/content/docs/react/guides/explicit.mdx

title: Explicit
description: Configure explicit rendering options for reCAPTCHA

## What is explicit and why do you need it?

The `explicit` parameter allows you to control how and where the reCAPTCHA widget is rendered. By default, reCAPTCHA automatically renders in specific locations, but with `explicit` you get full control over the rendering process.

## Configuring explicit for all reCAPTCHA types

The `explicit` parameter can be configured for all reCAPTCHA types (v2-checkbox, v2-invisible, v3). For detailed type definitions, refer to the provider interfaces:

- `GoogleReCaptchaV2CheckBoxProviderProps` - for v2-checkbox
- `GoogleReCaptchaV2InvisibleProviderProps` - for v2-invisible
- `GoogleReCaptchaV3ProviderProps` - for v3

## v2 сheckbox

For v2-checkbox, the `explicit` parameter is always `true` by default. This means reCAPTCHA won't render automatically - you need to explicitly place the `GoogleReCaptchaCheckbox` component where you want the widget to appear.

```tsx
<GoogleReCaptchaProvider type='v2-checkbox' siteKey='your_site_key'>
  <GoogleReCaptchaCheckbox />
</GoogleReCaptchaProvider>
```

If you prefer not to use the [`GoogleReCaptchaCheckbox` component](../references/GoogleReCaptchaCheckbox.mdx), you can configure the widget directly through the `explicit` [parameter](../references//GoogleReCaptchaProvider.mdx#v2-checkbox-props). This gives you more control over the rendering process:

```tsx
<GoogleReCaptchaProvider
  type='v2-checkbox'
  siteKey='your_site_key'
  explicit={{
    container: 'container',
    callback: (token) => console.log('Token:', token)
  }}
>
  <div id='container' />
</GoogleReCaptchaProvider>
```

## v3 and v2 Invisible

For v3 and v2-invisible, you can configure badge parameters through the `explicit` [object](../references/GoogleReCaptchaProvider.mdx#v3-props), or use `explicit: true` with the `GoogleReCaptchaBadge` component for custom placement. You can configure badge position and size through the `explicit` object:

```tsx
<GoogleReCaptchaProvider
  type='v3 | v2-invisible'
  siteKey='your_site_key'
  explicit={{
    container: 'container',
    badge: 'bottomleft',
    size: 'compact'
  }}
>
  <div id='container' />
</GoogleReCaptchaProvider>
```

### Using explicit

By default, reCAPTCHA automatically renders a badge in the bottom-right corner. If you want to control where the badge appears, use `explicit: true` and the [`GoogleReCaptchaBadge` component](../references/GoogleReCaptchaBadge.mdx):

```tsx
<GoogleReCaptchaProvider type='v3 | v2-invisible' siteKey='your_site_key' explicit>
  <GoogleReCaptchaBadge />
</GoogleReCaptchaProvider>
```

---

# fallback.mdx

Source: https://github.com/siberiacancode/google-recaptcha/blob/main/packages/docs/content/docs/react/guides/fallback.mdx

title: Fallback
description: Implementing an abstract fallback flow with two different reCAPTCHA types (e.g., v3 and v2)

import { Steps, Step } from 'fumadocs-ui/components/steps';

<Steps>
  <Step title="Add the provider">
    First, we need to initialize the main reCAPTCHA provider component. In these examples, we'll use reCAPTCHA v3 as a starting point for the flow:

    ```tsx
    import React from 'react';
    import { GoogleReCaptchaProvider } from '@google-recaptcha/react';

    export const App = () => (
      <GoogleReCaptchaProvider type='v3' siteKey='your_site_key'>
        ...
      </GoogleReCaptchaProvider>
    );
    ```

  </Step>

  <Step title="Create verification component">
    In our component, we want to perform verification by sending the reCAPTCHA token to our backend API.

    ```tsx twoslash
    import React from "react";
    import { useGoogleReCaptcha } from "@google-recaptcha/react";

    const App = () => {
      const googleReCaptcha = useGoogleReCaptcha();

      const onVerify = async () => {
        if (!googleReCaptcha.executeV3) {
          console.log("Execute recaptcha not available");
          return;
        }

        // [!code word:"action"]
        const token = await googleReCaptcha.executeV3("action");
      };

      return <button onClick={onVerify}>verify</button>;
    };
    ```

  </Step>

  <Step title="Show the fallback component">
    After receiving the token, call your backend validation; if it fails, you can trigger another reCAPTCHA version with its own `siteKey`.

    ```tsx twoslash
    import React from "react";
    import { useDisclosure } from "@siberiacancode/reactuse"; // [!code highlight]
    import { GoogleReCaptchaCheckbox, useGoogleReCaptcha } from "@google-recaptcha/react"; // [!code highlight]

    const App = () => {
      const googleReCaptcha = useGoogleReCaptcha();
      const fallbackRecaptcha = useDisclosure(); // [!code highlight]

      const onVerify = async () => {
        if (!googleReCaptcha.executeV3) {
          console.log("Execute recaptcha not available");
          return;
        }

        try {
          // [!code word:"action"]
          const token = await googleReCaptcha.executeV3("action");
          // your request with token
          const response = await fetch("/api/verify", {
            method: "POST",
            body: JSON.stringify({ token })
          });
          // ...
        } catch {
          fallbackRecaptcha.open();
        }
      };

      return (
        <>
          <button onClick={onVerify}>verify</button>
          {fallbackRecaptcha.opened && (
            <GoogleReCaptchaCheckbox
              // [!code word:"your_v2_site_key"]
              onChange={(token) => console.log(token)}
            />
          )}
        </>
      );
    };
    ```

  </Step>
</Steps>

---

# hide-badge.mdx

Source: https://github.com/siberiacancode/google-recaptcha/blob/main/packages/docs/content/docs/react/guides/hide-badge.mdx

title: Hide badge
description: Learn how to hide the reCAPTCHA badge while complying with Google's terms of service

Sometimes you may want to hide the reCAPTCHA badge to implement your own privacy policy and terms of service display. This is a common requirement for applications that need to maintain a specific design aesthetic or want to present their privacy information in a more integrated way.

Google officially allows hiding the badge, but with an important requirement: you must include the reCAPTCHA branding and privacy policy text in your application's privacy policy or terms of service. This ensures users are still informed about the use of reCAPTCHA while maintaining your desired design.

## Official solution

The official way to hide the badge is through CSS. Google provides a specific class that you can target to hide the badge while maintaining compliance with their terms of service. Here's how to implement it:

```css
.grecaptcha-badge {
  display: none !important;
}
```

You can add this CSS to your global styles or component-specific styles.

## Using the helper function

For convenience, we provide a helper function `hideGoogleReCaptchaBadge` and [`generateGoogleReCaptchaHiddenBadgeStyles`](../references/generateGoogleReCaptchaHiddenBadgeStyles.mdx) that handles the badge hiding for you.

---

# theme.mdx

Source: https://github.com/siberiacancode/google-recaptcha/blob/main/packages/docs/content/docs/react/guides/theme.mdx

title: Theme
description: Learn how to customize the appearance of reCAPTCHA widgets

The google recaptcha provides two themes: "light" and "dark". We can set the theme in the provider configuration for v3 and v2 invisible or v2 checkbox.

```tsx
<GoogleReCaptchaProvider
  type='v3 | v2-checkbox | v2-invisible'
  siteKey='your_site_key'
  theme='dark | light' //[!code highlight]
>
  {children}
</GoogleReCaptchaProvider>
```

### Badge customization

For v2 invisible and v3, customize the badge position and size:

```tsx
<GoogleReCaptchaProvider
  type='v3 | v2-invisible'
  siteKey='your_site_key'
  explicit={{
    badge: 'bottomright | bottomleft | inline', //[!code highlight]
    size: 'normal | compact' //[!code highlight]
  }}
>
  {children}
</GoogleReCaptchaProvider>
```

# index.mdx

Source: https://github.com/siberiacancode/google-recaptcha/blob/main/packages/docs/content/docs/react/index.mdx

title: Installation
description: Install the react recaptcha package

import { ReactUseBanner } from '@/app/(components)/reactuse-banner';

The React package provides a comprehensive solution for integrating Google reCAPTCHA into React applications. Built specifically for React, it offers hooks, components, and providers that seamlessly integrate with your React workflow while supporting all reCAPTCHA versions including [v3](./versions/v3), [v2-invisible](./versions/v2-invisible), and [v2-checkbox](./versions/v2-checkbox).

## Installation

Install the React package using your preferred package manager:

```package-install
npm install @google-recaptcha/react
```

## Setup

All reCAPTCHA functionality requires wrapping your application with the `GoogleReCaptchaProvider`. This provider manages the reCAPTCHA script loading and provides context to child components.

```tsx
import { GoogleReCaptchaProvider } from '@google-recaptcha/react';

export const App = () => (
  <GoogleReCaptchaProvider type='v3 | v2-checkbox | v2-invisible' siteKey='your_site_key'>
    ...
  </GoogleReCaptchaProvider>
);
```

<ReactUseBanner />

# next.mdx

Source: https://github.com/siberiacancode/google-recaptcha/blob/main/packages/docs/content/docs/react/integrations/next.mdx

title: Next.js
description: Integrate the react google recaptcha with Next.js

import { Steps, Step } from 'fumadocs-ui/components/steps';

<Steps>
  <Step title="Installation">
    Install the required package using your preferred package manager:

    ```package-install
    npm install @google-recaptcha/react
    ```

    <Callout>
      This package provides React components and hooks for client-side reCAPTCHA integration.
    </Callout>

  </Step>

  <Step title="Create wrapper">
    For Next.js applications, you have few options for reCAPTCHA integration, but first you need create client provider component

    ```tsx title="app/google-recaptcha-provider.tsx"
    "use client";

    import type { ComponentProps } from "react";
    import { GoogleReCaptchaProvider as _GoogleReCaptchaProvider } from "@google-recaptcha/react";

    export type ReCaptchaProviderProps = ComponentProps<typeof _GoogleReCaptchaProvider>;

    export const GoogleReCaptchaProvider = (props) => (
      <_GoogleReCaptchaProvider {...props} />
    );
    ```

  </Step>

  <Step title="Add provider">
    Add provider to your layout component

    ```tsx title="app/layout.tsx"
    import type { ReactNode } from "react";
    import { GoogleReCaptchaProvider } from "./google-recaptcha-provider"; // [!code highlight]

    interface RootLayoutProps {
      children: ReactNode;
    }

    const RootLayout = ({ children }: RootLayoutProps) => (
      <html lang="en">
        <body>
          <main>
            <GoogleReCaptchaProvider type="v3" siteKey="your_site_key">
              {children}
            </GoogleReCaptchaProvider>
          </main>
        </body>
      </html>
    );

    export default RootLayout;
    ```

  </Step>

  <Step title="Use recapthca in your components">
    ```tsx
    const googleReCaptcha = useGoogleReCaptcha();

    const onSubmit = async () => {
      const token = await googleReCaptcha.executeV3('action');
      ...
    }
    ```

  </Step>
</Steps>

## Optimize script loading

You can optimize performance by pre-loading the reCAPTCHA script using Next.js Script component combined with the core utility function. The `GoogleReCaptchaProvider` automatically detects if the reCAPTCHA script is already loaded and will not add a duplicate script tag

```tsx title="app/layout.tsx"
import type { ReactNode } from 'react';
import Script from 'next/script';

import { GoogleReCaptchaProvider } from './google-recaptcha-provider';

interface RootLayoutProps {
  children: ReactNode;
}

const RootLayout = ({ children }: RootLayoutProps) => {
  const scriptSrc = generateGoogleReCaptchaScriptSrc({
    isEnterprise: false,
    render: 'your_site_key',
    hl: 'en'
  });

  return (
    <html lang='en'>
      <head>
        <Script src={scriptSrc} strategy='afterInteractive' />
      </head>
      <body>
        <main>
          <GoogleReCaptchaProvider type='v3' siteKey='your_site_key'>
            {children}
          </GoogleReCaptchaProvider>
        </main>
      </body>
    </html>
  );
};

export default RootLayout;
```

title: Vite

import { Steps, Step } from 'fumadocs-ui/components/steps';

    ```package-install
    npm install @google-recaptcha/react
    ```

  </Step>

  <Step title="Provider Setup">
    Wrap your application with the `GoogleReCaptchaProvider` in your root component:

    ```tsx
    // src/main.tsx
    import React from 'react';
    import ReactDOM from 'react-dom/client';
    import { GoogleReCaptchaProvider } from '@google-recaptcha/react'; // [!code highlight]

    import App from './App';

    ReactDOM.createRoot(document.getElementById('root')!).render(
      <React.StrictMode>
        <GoogleReCaptchaProvider
          type="v3"
          siteKey="your_site_key"
        >
          <App />
        </GoogleReCaptchaProvider>
      </React.StrictMode>
    );
    ```

  </Step>

  <Step title="Client Component Usage">
    Create a component to use reCAPTCHA:

    ```tsx
    import type { FormEvent } from 'react';
    import { useGoogleReCaptcha } from '@google-recaptcha/react';

    export const Form = () => {
      const googleReCaptcha = useGoogleReCaptcha();

      const onSubmit = async (event: FormEvent) => {
        event.preventDefault();

        const token = await googleReCaptcha.executeV3('action');
        ...
      };

      return (
        <form onSubmit={onSubmit}>
          ...
          <button type="submit">Submit</button>
        </form>
      );
    }
    ```

  </Step>
</Steps>

# generateGoogleReCaptchaScriptSrc.mdx

Source: https://github.com/siberiacancode/google-recaptcha/blob/main/packages/docs/content/docs/react/references/generateGoogleReCaptchaScriptSrc.mdx

title: generateGoogleReCaptchaScriptSrc
description: Utility function for generating Google reCAPTCHA script source URL

```ts
const scriptSrc = generateGoogleReCaptchaScriptSrc({
  host,
  isEnterprise,
  render,
  hl,
  badge
});
```

## Parameters

| Parameter      | Type                                        | Required | Default        | Description                                        |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------- | -------- | -------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `host`         | `string`                                    | -        | `'google.com'` | The host for the script source URL                 |
| `isEnterprise` | `boolean`                                   | -        | `false`        | Whether to use the enterprise version of reCAPTCHA |
| `render`       | `string`                                    | Yes      | -              | The render parameter for the script source URL     |
| `hl`           | `string`                                    | -        | -              | The language code for the reCAPTCHA widget         |
| `badge`        | `'bottomright' \| 'bottomleft' \| 'inline'` | -        | -              | The position of the reCAPTCHA badge                |

## Return

Returns a string containing the complete URL for the Google reCAPTCHA script.

---

| ----------- | ------------------------- | -------- | --------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------- |
| `id`        | `string`                  | -        | `'google-recaptcha-checkbox-container'` | The ID of the checkbox container                      |
| `language`  | `string`                  | -        | -                                       | The language for the reCAPTCHA widget                 |
| `theme`     | `'light' \| 'dark'`       | -        | `'light'`                               | The color theme of the widget                         |
| `onChange`  | `(token: string) => void` | -        | -                                       | Callback function when verification is successful     |
| `onError`   | `() => void`              | -        | -                                       | Callback function when reCAPTCHA encounters an error  |
| `onExpired` | `() => void`              | -        | -                                       | Callback function when the reCAPTCHA response expires |

The component extends the standard `div` props

# GoogleReCaptchaProvider.mdx

Source: https://github.com/siberiacancode/google-recaptcha/blob/main/packages/docs/content/docs/react/references/GoogleReCaptchaProvider.mdx

title: GoogleReCaptchaProvider
description: Provider component for Google reCAPTCHA integration in React applications

```tsx
<GoogleReCaptchaProvider
  type
  siteKey
  language
  scriptProps
  isEnterprise
  host
  theme
  explicit
  onLoad
  onError
>
  {children}
</GoogleReCaptchaProvider>
```

## Props

### Common Props

| Prop           | Type                                      | Required | Default | Description                                    |
| -------------- | ----------------------------------------- | -------- | ------- | ---------------------------------------------- |
| `type`         | `'v2-checkbox' \| 'v2-invisible' \| 'v3'` | Yes      | -       | The type of reCAPTCHA to use                   |
| `siteKey`      | `string`                                  | Yes      | -       | Your Google reCAPTCHA site key                 |
| `language`     | `string`                                  | -        | -       | Language code for the reCAPTCHA widget         |
| `scriptProps`  | `GoogleReCaptcha.Script`                  | -        | -       | Additional properties for the reCAPTCHA script |
| `isEnterprise` | `boolean`                                 | -        | `false` | Whether to use reCAPTCHA Enterprise            |
| `host`         | `string`                                  | -        | -       | Custom host for the reCAPTCHA script           |
| `theme`        | `'light' \| 'dark'`                       | -        | `light` | Theme of the reCAPTCHA widget                  |
| `onLoad`       | `(instance: ReCaptchaInstance) => void`   | -        | -       | Callback function when reCAPTCHA is loaded     |
| `onError`      | `() => void`                              | -        | -       | Callback function when an error occurs         |

### v3 props

| Prop                       | Type                                        | Required | Default | Description                                  |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- | -------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| `explicit.badge`           | `'bottomright' \| 'bottomleft' \| 'inline'` | -        | -       | Position of the reCAPTCHA badge              |
| `explicit.tabIndex`        | `number`                                    | -        | -       | Tab index for the reCAPTCHA widget           |
| `explicit.callback`        | `(token: string) => void`                   | -        | -       | Callback when verification is successful     |
| `explicit.errorCallback`   | `() => void`                                | -        | -       | Callback when reCAPTCHA encounters an error  |
| `explicit.expiredCallback` | `() => void`                                | -        | -       | Callback when the reCAPTCHA response expires |

### v2 checkbox props

| Prop                       | Type                      | Required | Default | Description                                  |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------- | -------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| `explicit.container`       | `string`                  | Yes      | -       | Container ID for the reCAPTCHA widget        |
| `explicit.action`          | `string`                  | -        | -       | Action name for the reCAPTCHA                |
| `explicit.size`            | `'normal' \| 'compact'`   | -        | -       | Size of the reCAPTCHA widget                 |
| `explicit.tabIndex`        | `number`                  | -        | -       | Tab index for the reCAPTCHA widget           |
| `explicit.callback`        | `(token: string) => void` | -        | -       | Callback when verification is successful     |
| `explicit.errorCallback`   | `() => void`              | -        | -       | Callback when reCAPTCHA encounters an error  |
| `explicit.expiredCallback` | `() => void`              | -        | -       | Callback when the reCAPTCHA response expires |

### v2 invisible props

| Prop                       | Type                                        | Required | Default | Description                                  |
| -------------------------- | ------------------------------------------- | -------- | ------- | -------------------------------------------- |
| `explicit.badge`           | `'bottomright' \| 'bottomleft' \| 'inline'` | -        | -       | Position of the reCAPTCHA badge              |
| `explicit.tabIndex`        | `number`                                    | -        | -       | Tab index for the reCAPTCHA widget           |
| `explicit.callback`        | `(token: string) => void`                   | -        | -       | Callback when verification is successful     |
| `explicit.errorCallback`   | `() => void`                                | -        | -       | Callback when reCAPTCHA encounters an error  |
| `explicit.expiredCallback` | `() => void`                                | -        | -       | Callback when the reCAPTCHA response expires |

## Context values

| Property             | Type                                   | Description                                                                                              |
| -------------------- | -------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `instance`           | `ReCaptchaInstance \| null`            | The reCAPTCHA instance.                                                                                  |
| `isLoading`          | `boolean`                              | Whether the reCAPTCHA script is still loading.                                                           |
| `language`           | `string`                               | The language code used for reCAPTCHA.                                                                    |
| `siteKey`            | `string`                               | The site key used for reCAPTCHA.                                                                         |
| `executeV3`          | `(action?: string) => Promise<string>` | Executes reCAPTCHA v3 verification. Returns a promise that resolves to the verification token.           |
| `executeV2Invisible` | `() => Promise<string>`                | Executes reCAPTCHA v2 invisible verification. Returns a promise that resolves to the verification token. |
| `reset`              | `() => void`                           | Resets the reCAPTCHA widget.                                                                             |
| `getResponse`        | `() => string`                         | Gets the current reCAPTCHA response token.                                                               |
| `render`             | `() => void`                           | Renders the reCAPTCHA widget.                                                                            |

# useGoogleReCaptcha.mdx

Source: https://github.com/siberiacancode/google-recaptcha/blob/main/packages/docs/content/docs/react/references/useGoogleReCaptcha.mdx

title: useGoogleReCaptcha
description: Hook for accessing reCAPTCHA functionality in React components

```tsx
const {
  instance,
  isLoading,
  language,
  siteKey,
  executeV3,
  executeV2Invisible,
  reset,
  getResponse,
  render
} = useGoogleReCaptcha();
```

## Values

| Property             | Type                                                                                                        | Description                                                                                              |
| -------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `instance`           | `ReCaptchaInstance \| null`                                                                                 | The reCAPTCHA instance.                                                                                  |
| `isLoading`          | `boolean`                                                                                                   | Whether the reCAPTCHA script is still loading.                                                           |
| `language`           | `string`                                                                                                    | The language code used for reCAPTCHA.                                                                    |
| `siteKey`            | `string`                                                                                                    | The site key used for reCAPTCHA.                                                                         |
| `executeV3`          | `(action?: string) => Promise<string>`                                                                      | Executes reCAPTCHA v3 verification. Returns a promise that resolves to the verification token.           |
| `executeV2Invisible` | `() => Promise<string>`                                                                                     | Executes reCAPTCHA v2 invisible verification. Returns a promise that resolves to the verification token. |
| `reset`              | `() => void`                                                                                                | Resets the reCAPTCHA widget.                                                                             |
| `getResponse`        | `() => string`                                                                                              | Gets the current reCAPTCHA response token.                                                               |
| `render`             | `(container: Container, parameters?: GoogleReCaptcha.Parameters, inherit?: boolean) => number \| undefined` | Renders the reCAPTCHA widget and returns its widget id.                                                  |

# enterprise.mdx

Source: https://github.com/siberiacancode/google-recaptcha/blob/main/packages/docs/content/docs/react/versions/enterprise.mdx

title: enterprise
description: The Enterprise mode provides enhanced security features, advanced analytics, and better customization options for businesses

Google reCAPTCHA Enterprise provides enhanced security features, advanced analytics, and better customization options for businesses. It offers improved bot detection, detailed risk analysis, and enterprise-grade support.

## Provider Setup

To use Enterprise features, you need to enable the `isEnterprise` flag in the provider:

```tsx
import React from 'react';
import { GoogleReCaptchaProvider } from '@google-recaptcha/react';

export const App = () => (
  // [!code word:isEnterprise]
  <GoogleReCaptchaProvider type='v3 | v2-checkbox' siteKey='your_enterprise_site_key' isEnterprise>
    ...
  </GoogleReCaptchaProvider>
);
```

## Usage

### V3 Enterprise

Enterprise mode enhances v3 reCAPTCHA with additional risk assessment capabilities and detailed analytics:

```tsx twoslash
import React from 'react';
import { useGoogleReCaptcha } from '@google-recaptcha/react';

const App = () => {
  const googleReCaptcha = useGoogleReCaptcha();

  const onVerify = async () => {
    if (!googleReCaptcha.executeV3) {
      console.log('Execute recaptcha not available');
      return;
    }

    // [!code word:"action"]
    const token = await googleReCaptcha.executeV3('action');
  };

  return <button onClick={onVerify}>verify</button>;
};
```

### V2 Checkbox Enterprise

Enterprise mode for v2 checkbox provides enhanced security and analytics:

```tsx twoslash
import React from 'react';
import { GoogleReCaptchaCheckbox } from '@google-recaptcha/react';

const App = () => (
  <GoogleReCaptchaCheckbox
    // [!code word:"some action"]
    action='some action'
    onChange={(token) => console.log(token)}
  />
);
```

# v2-checkbox.mdx

Source: https://github.com/siberiacancode/google-recaptcha/blob/main/packages/docs/content/docs/react/versions/v2-checkbox.mdx

title: v2 сheckbox
description: The Google reCAPTCHA v2 checkbox is a reCAPTCHA version that displays a checkbox to the user. It is used to verify that the user is a human and not a bot.

import { ReactDemo } from '@/app/(components)/demos';

## Demo

<ReactDemo type='v2-checkbox' />

## Provider Setup

All reCAPTCHA functionality requires wrapping your application with the `GoogleReCaptchaProvider`. This provider manages the reCAPTCHA script loading and provides context to child components.

```tsx twoslash
import React from 'react';
import { GoogleReCaptchaProvider } from '@google-recaptcha/react';

export const App = () => (
  // [!code word:"v2-checkbox"]
  <GoogleReCaptchaProvider type='v2-checkbox' siteKey='your_site_key'>
    ...
  </GoogleReCaptchaProvider>
);
```

## Usage

When a user interacts with the [Google ReCaptcha v2 checkbox](https://developers.google.com/recaptcha/docs/display), advanced algorithms analyze their behavior to distinguish between humans and bots. If the system suspects suspicious activity, additional challenges may be presented, such as image selections or puzzle-solving tasks.

```tsx twoslash
import React from 'react';
import { GoogleReCaptchaCheckbox } from '@google-recaptcha/react';

const App = () => <GoogleReCaptchaCheckbox onChange={(token) => console.log(token)} />;
```

## Enterprise Mode

Google reCAPTCHA Enterprise provides enhanced security features, advanced analytics, and better customization options for businesses. It offers improved bot detection, detailed risk analysis, and enterprise-grade support.

```tsx
// [!code word:isEnterprise]
<GoogleReCaptchaProvider type='v2-checkbox' siteKey='your_enterprise_site_key' isEnterprise>
  <App />
</GoogleReCaptchaProvider>
```

After enabling enterprise mode, you can use the `GoogleReCaptchaCheckbox` component to set the action for the checkbox.

```tsx twoslash
import React from 'react';
import { GoogleReCaptchaCheckbox } from '@google-recaptcha/react';

const App = () => (
  <GoogleReCaptchaCheckbox
    // [!code word:"some action"]
    action='some action'
    onChange={(token) => console.log(token)}
  />
);
```

# v2-invisible.mdx

title: v2 invisible
description: The Google reCAPTCHA v2 invisible is a reCAPTCHA version that runs in the background without requiring user interaction. It is used to verify that the user is a human and not a bot.

import { ReactDemo } from '@/app/(components)/demos';

## Demo

<ReactDemo type='v2-invisible' />

## Provider Setup

```tsx twoslash
import React from 'react';

  </GoogleReCaptchaProvider>

```

## Usage

[Google ReCaptcha v2 invisible](https://developers.google.com/recaptcha/docs/display) does not require users to solve any puzzles or enter any codes. Instead, it runs in the background and analyzes user behavior on the web page to determine if they are genuine users or potential bots.

```tsx twoslash
import React from 'react';
import { useGoogleReCaptcha } from '@google-recaptcha/react';

const App = () => {

};
```

# v3.mdx

Source: https://github.com/siberiacancode/google-recaptcha/blob/main/packages/docs/content/docs/react/versions/v3.mdx

title: v3
description: The Google reCAPTCHA v3 returns a score for each request without user friction. The score is based on interactions with your site and enables you to take an appropriate action for your site.

import { ReactDemo } from '@/app/(components)/demos';

## Demo

<ReactDemo type='v3' />

## Provider Setup

All reCAPTCHA functionality requires wrapping your application with the `GoogleReCaptchaProvider`. This provider manages the reCAPTCHA script loading and provides context to child components.

```tsx twoslash
import React from 'react';
import { GoogleReCaptchaProvider } from '@google-recaptcha/react';

export const App = () => (
  // [!code word:"v3"]
  <GoogleReCaptchaProvider type='v3' siteKey='your_site_key'>
    ...
  </GoogleReCaptchaProvider>
);
```

## Usage

[Google ReCaptcha v3](https://developers.google.com/recaptcha/docs/v3) returns a score for each request without user friction. The score is based on interactions with your site and enables you to take an appropriate action for your site.

```tsx twoslash
import React from 'react';
import { useGoogleReCaptcha } from '@google-recaptcha/react';

const App = () => {
  const googleReCaptcha = useGoogleReCaptcha();

  const onVerify = async () => {
    if (!googleReCaptcha.executeV3) {
      console.log('Execute recaptcha not available');
      return;
    }

    // [!code word:executeV3]
    const token = await googleReCaptcha.executeV3('action');
  };

  return <button onClick={onVerify}>verify</button>;
};
```

## Enterprise Mode

Google reCAPTCHA Enterprise provides enhanced security features, advanced analytics, and better customization options for businesses. It offers improved bot detection, detailed risk analysis, and enterprise-grade support.

```tsx
// [!code word:isEnterprise]
<GoogleReCaptchaProvider type='v3' siteKey='your_enterprise_site_key' isEnterprise>
  <App />
</GoogleReCaptchaProvider>
```

After enabling enterprise mode, you can use the `executeV3` function to set some actions for better risk assessment.

```tsx twoslash
import React from 'react';
import { useGoogleReCaptcha } from '@google-recaptcha/react';

const App = () => {
  const googleReCaptcha = useGoogleReCaptcha();

  const onVerify = async () => {
    if (!googleReCaptcha.executeV3) {
      console.log('Execute recaptcha not available');
      return;
    }

    // [!code word:"action"]
    const token = await googleReCaptcha.executeV3('action');
  };

  return <button onClick={onVerify}>verify</button>;
};
```

# explicit.mdx

Source: https://github.com/siberiacancode/google-recaptcha/blob/main/packages/docs/content/docs/vue/guides/explicit.mdx

title: Explicit
description: Configure explicit rendering options for reCAPTCHA

## What is explicit and why do you need it?

The `explicit` parameter allows you to control how and where the reCAPTCHA widget is rendered. By default, reCAPTCHA automatically renders in specific locations, but with `explicit` you get full control over the rendering process.

## Configuring explicit for all reCAPTCHA types

The `explicit` parameter can be configured for all reCAPTCHA types (v2-checkbox, v2-invisible, v3). For detailed type definitions, refer to the provider interfaces:

- `GoogleReCaptchaV2CheckBoxOptions` - for v2-checkbox
- `GoogleReCaptchaV2InvisibleOptions` - for v2-invisible
- `GoogleReCaptchaV3Options` - for v3

## v2 сheckbox

For v2-checkbox, the `explicit` parameter is always `true` by default. This means reCAPTCHA won't render automatically - you need to explicitly place the `GoogleReCaptchaCheckbox` component where you want the widget to appear.

```vue tab="Component"
<GoogleReCaptchaProvider type="v2-checkbox" siteKey="your_site_key">
  <GoogleReCaptchaCheckbox />
</GoogleReCaptchaProvider>
```

```vue tab="Composable"
<script setup>
import { useGoogleReCaptchaProvider } from '@google-recaptcha/vue';

useGoogleReCaptchaProvider({
  type: 'v2-checkbox',
  siteKey: 'your_site_key'
});
</script>
```

If you prefer not to use the [`GoogleReCaptchaCheckbox` component](../references/GoogleReCaptchaCheckbox.mdx), you can configure the widget directly through the `explicit` [parameter](../references/GoogleReCaptchaProvider.mdx#v2-checkbox-props). This gives you more control over the rendering process:

```vue tab="Component"
<GoogleReCaptchaProvider
  type="v2-checkbox"
  siteKey="your_site_key"
  :explicit="{
    container: 'container',
    callback: (token) => console.log('Token:', token)
  }"
>
  <div id="container" />
</GoogleReCaptchaProvider>
```

```vue tab="Composable"
<script setup>
import { useGoogleReCaptchaProvider } from '@google-recaptcha/vue';

useGoogleReCaptchaProvider({
  type: 'v2-checkbox',
  siteKey: 'your_site_key',
  explicit: {
    container: 'container',
    callback: (token) => console.log('Token:', token)
  }
});
</script>
```

## v3 and v2 Invisible

For v3 and v2-invisible, you can configure badge parameters through the `explicit` [object](../references/GoogleReCaptchaProvider.mdx#v3-props), or use `explicit: true` with the `GoogleReCaptchaBadge` component for custom placement. You can configure badge position and size through the `explicit` object:

```vue tab="Component"
<GoogleReCaptchaProvider
  type="v3 | v2-invisible"
  siteKey="your_site_key"
  :explicit="{
    container: 'container',
    badge: 'bottomleft',
    size: 'compact'
  }"
>
  <div id="container" />
</GoogleReCaptchaProvider>
```

```vue tab="Composable"
<script setup>
import { useGoogleReCaptchaProvider } from '@google-recaptcha/vue';

useGoogleReCaptchaProvider({
  type: 'v3',
  siteKey: 'your_site_key',
  explicit: {
    container: 'container',
    badge: 'bottomleft',
    size: 'compact'
  }
});
</script>
```

### Using explicit

By default, reCAPTCHA automatically renders a badge in the bottom-right corner. If you want to control where the badge appears, use `explicit: true` and the [`GoogleReCaptchaBadge` component](../references/GoogleReCaptchaBadge.mdx):

```vue tab="Component"
<GoogleReCaptchaProvider type="v3 | v2-invisible" siteKey="your_site_key" explicit>
  <GoogleReCaptchaBadge />
</GoogleReCaptchaProvider>
```

```vue tab="Composable"
<script setup>
import { useGoogleReCaptchaProvider } from '@google-recaptcha/vue';

useGoogleReCaptchaProvider({
  type: 'v3',
  siteKey: 'your_site_key',
  explicit: true
});
</script>
```

---

# fallback.mdx

Source: https://github.com/siberiacancode/google-recaptcha/blob/main/packages/docs/content/docs/vue/guides/fallback.mdx

title: Fallback
description: Implementing an abstract fallback flow with two different reCAPTCHA types (e.g., v3 and v2)

import { Steps, Step } from 'fumadocs-ui/components/steps';

<Steps>
  <Step title="Add the provider">
    You always need a `GoogleReCaptchaProvider`. In Vue you can set it up with a component, composable, or plugin:

    ```vue tab="Component"
    <template>
      <GoogleReCaptchaProvider type="v3" siteKey="your_site_key">
        <slot />
      </GoogleReCaptchaProvider>
    </template>

    <script setup>
    import { GoogleReCaptchaProvider } from '@google-recaptcha/vue';
    </script>
    ```

    ```vue tab="Composable"
    <script setup>
    import { useGoogleReCaptchaProvider } from '@google-recaptcha/vue';

    useGoogleReCaptchaProvider({
      type: 'v3',
      siteKey: 'your_site_key'
    });
    </script>
    ```

    ```vue tab="Plugin"
    <script setup>
    import { createApp } from 'vue';
    import { googleReCaptcha } from '@google-recaptcha/vue';

    const app = createApp(App);

    app.use(googleReCaptcha, {
      type: 'v3',
      siteKey: 'your_site_key'
    });
    </script>
    ```

  </Step>

  <Step title="Create verification component">
    In our component, we want to perform verification by sending the reCAPTCHA token to our backend API.

    ```vue tab="Composable"
    <script setup>
    import { useGoogleReCaptcha } from '@google-recaptcha/vue';

    const googleReCaptcha = useGoogleReCaptcha();

    const onVerify = async () => {
      if (!googleReCaptcha.executeV3) {
        console.log('Execute recaptcha not available');
        return;
      }

      // [!code word:executeV3]
      const token = await googleReCaptcha.executeV3('action');
    };
    </script>

    <template>
      <button @click="onVerify">verify</button>
    </template>
    ```

    ```vue tab="Component"
    <script setup>
    import { GoogleReCaptchaV3 } from '@google-recaptcha/vue';

    const onVerify = (token) => {
      ...
    };
    </script>

    <template>
      <GoogleReCaptchaV3 action="custom_action" @verify="onVerify" />
    </template>
    ```

  </Step>

  <Step title="Show the fallback component">
    After receiving the token, call your backend validation; if it fails, you can trigger another reCAPTCHA version with its own `siteKey`.

    ```vue tab="Composable"
    <script setup>
    import { ref } from 'vue';
    import { GoogleReCaptchaCheckbox, useGoogleReCaptcha } from '@google-recaptcha/vue';

    const showFallback = ref(false);
    const googleReCaptcha = useGoogleReCaptcha();

    const onVerify = async () => {
      if (!googleReCaptcha.executeV3) {
        console.log('Execute recaptcha not available');
        return;
      }

      // [!code word:executeV3]
      const token = await googleReCaptcha.executeV3('action');

      try {
        // your request with token
        const response = await fetch('/api/verify', {
          method: 'POST',
          body: JSON.stringify({ token })
        });
        // ...
      } catch {
        showFallback.value = true;
      }
    };
    </script>

    <template>
      <button @click="onVerify">verify</button>
      <GoogleReCaptchaCheckbox
        v-if="showFallback"
        siteKey="your_v2_site_key"
        @change="(token) => console.log(token)"
      />
    </template>
    ```

    ```vue tab="Component"
    <script setup>
    import { ref } from 'vue';
    import { GoogleReCaptchaCheckbox, GoogleReCaptchaV3 } from '@google-recaptcha/vue';

    const showFallback = ref(false);

    const onVerify = async (token) => {
      try {
        // your request with token
        const response = await fetch('/api/verify', {
          method: 'POST',
          body: JSON.stringify({ token })
        });
        // ...
      } catch {
        showFallback.value = true;
      }
    };
    </script>

    <template>
      <GoogleReCaptchaV3 action="custom_action" @verify="onVerify" />
      <GoogleReCaptchaCheckbox
        v-if="showFallback"
        siteKey="your_v2_site_key"
        @change="(token) => console.log(token)"
      />
    </template>
    ```

  </Step>
</Steps>

---

# hide-badge.mdx

Source: https://github.com/siberiacancode/google-recaptcha/blob/main/packages/docs/content/docs/vue/guides/hide-badge.mdx

title: Hide badge
description: Learn how to hide the reCAPTCHA badge while complying with Google's terms of service

Sometimes you may want to hide the reCAPTCHA badge to implement your own privacy policy and terms of service display. This is a common requirement for applications that need to maintain a specific design aesthetic or want to present their privacy information in a more integrated way.

Google officially allows hiding the badge, but with an important requirement: you must include the reCAPTCHA branding and privacy policy text in your application's privacy policy or terms of service. This ensures users are still informed about the use of reCAPTCHA while maintaining your desired design.

## Official solution

The official way to hide the badge is through CSS. Google provides a specific class that you can target to hide the badge while maintaining compliance with their terms of service. Here's how to implement it:

```css
.grecaptcha-badge {
  display: none !important;
}
```

You can add this CSS to your global styles or component-specific styles.

## Using the helper function

For convenience, we provide a helper function `hideGoogleReCaptchaBadge` and [`generateGoogleReCaptchaHiddenBadgeStyles`](../references/generateGoogleReCaptchaHiddenBadgeStyles.mdx) that handles the badge hiding for you.

---

# theme.mdx

Source: https://github.com/siberiacancode/google-recaptcha/blob/main/packages/docs/content/docs/vue/guides/theme.mdx

title: Theme
description: Learn how to customize the appearance of reCAPTCHA widgets

The google recaptcha provides two themes: "light" and "dark". We can set the theme in the provider configuration for v3 and v2 invisible or v2 checkbox.

```vue tab="Component"
<GoogleReCaptchaProvider
  type="v3 | v2-checkbox | v2-invisible"
  siteKey="your_site_key"
  theme="dark | light" //[!code highlight]
>
  <slot />
</GoogleReCaptchaProvider>
```

```vue tab="Composable"
<script setup>
import { useGoogleReCaptchaProvider } from '@google-recaptcha/vue';

useGoogleReCaptchaProvider({
  type: 'v3',
  siteKey: 'your_site_key',
  theme: 'dark | light' //[!code highlight]
});
</script>
```

```vue tab="Plugin"
<script setup>
import { createApp } from 'vue';
import { googleReCaptcha } from '@google-recaptcha/vue';

const app = createApp(App);

app.use(googleReCaptcha, {
  type: 'v3',
  siteKey: 'your_site_key',
  theme: 'dark | light' //[!code highlight]
});
</script>
```

For v2 invisible and v3, customize the badge position and size:

```vue tab="Component"
<GoogleReCaptchaProvider
  type="v3 | v2-invisible"
  siteKey="your_site_key"
  :explicit="{
    badge: 'bottomright | bottomleft | inline', //[!code highlight]
    size: 'normal | compact' //[!code highlight]
  }"
>
  <slot />
</GoogleReCaptchaProvider>
```

```vue tab="Composable"
  type: 'v3',
  siteKey: 'your_site_key',
  explicit: {
    badge: 'bottomright | bottomleft | inline', //[!code highlight]
    size: 'normal | compact' //[!code highlight]
  }
});
</script>
```

```vue tab="Plugin"
<script setup>
import { createApp } from 'vue';
import { googleReCaptcha } from '@google-recaptcha/vue';

const app = createApp(App);

  type: 'v3',
  siteKey: 'your_site_key',

  }
```

# index.mdx

Source: https://github.com/siberiacancode/google-recaptcha/blob/main/packages/docs/content/docs/vue/index.mdx

title: Installation
description: Install the vue recaptcha package

The Vue package provides a comprehensive solution for integrating Google reCAPTCHA into Vue applications. Built specifically for Vue, it offers composables, components, and plugins that seamlessly integrate with your Vue workflow while supporting all reCAPTCHA versions including [v3](./versions/v3), [v2-invisible](./versions/v2-invisible), and [v2-checkbox](./versions/v2-checkbox).

## Installation

Install the Vue package using your preferred package manager:

```package-install
npm install @google-recaptcha/vue
```

## Setup

All reCAPTCHA functionality requires wrapping your application with the `GoogleReCaptchaProvider`. This provider manages the reCAPTCHA script loading and provides context to child components.

```vue tab="Plugin"
<script setup>
import { createApp } from 'vue';
import { googleReCaptcha } from '@google-recaptcha/vue';

const app = createApp(App);

app.use(googleReCaptcha, {
  type: 'v3',
  siteKey: 'your_site_key'
});
</script>
```

```vue tab="Component"
<template>
  <GoogleReCaptchaProvider type="v3 | v2-checkbox | v2-invisible" siteKey="your_site_key">
    <slot />
  </GoogleReCaptchaProvider>
</template>

<script setup>
import { GoogleReCaptchaProvider } from '@google-recaptcha/vue';
</script>
```

```vue tab="Composable"
<script setup>
import { useGoogleReCaptchaProvider } from '@google-recaptcha/vue';

useGoogleReCaptchaProvider({
  type: 'v3',
  siteKey: 'your_site_key'
});
</script>
```

# nuxt.mdx

Source: https://github.com/siberiacancode/google-recaptcha/blob/main/packages/docs/content/docs/vue/integrations/nuxt.mdx

title: Nuxt.js
description: Integrate the vue google recaptcha with Nuxt.js

import { Steps, Step } from 'fumadocs-ui/components/steps';

<Steps>
  <Step title="Installation">
    Install the required package using your preferred package manager:

    ```package-install
    npm install @google-recaptcha/vue
    ```

    <Callout>
      This package provides Vue components and composables for client-side reCAPTCHA integration.
    </Callout>

  </Step>

  <Step title="Create plugin">
    Create a Nuxt plugin to initialize reCAPTCHA:

    ```ts title="plugins/google-recaptcha.ts"
    import { googleReCaptcha } from '@google-recaptcha/vue'

    export default defineNuxtPlugin((nuxtApp) => {
      nuxtApp.vueApp.use(googleReCaptcha, {
        type: 'v3',
        siteKey: 'your_site_key'
      })
    })
    ```

  </Step>

  <Step title="Use reCAPTCHA in your components">
    ```vue
    <template>
      <form @submit.prevent="onSubmit">
        ...
        <button type="submit">Submit</button>
      </form>
    </template>

    <script setup>
    import { useGoogleReCaptcha } from '@google-recaptcha/vue'

    const googleReCaptcha = useGoogleReCaptcha()

    const onSubmit = async () => {
      const token = await googleReCaptcha.executeV3('action')
      ...
    }
    </script>
    ```

  </Step>
</Steps>

## Optimize script loading

You can optimize performance by pre-loading the reCAPTCHA script using Nuxt's `useHead` composable combined with the core utility function. The `googleReCaptcha` plugin automatically detects if the reCAPTCHA script is already loaded and will not add a duplicate script tag.

```ts title="plugins/google-recaptcha.ts"
import { googleReCaptcha } from '@google-recaptcha/vue';
import { generateGoogleReCaptchaScriptSrc } from '@google-recaptcha/core';

export default defineNuxtPlugin((nuxtApp) => {
  const scriptSrc = generateGoogleReCaptchaScriptSrc({
    isEnterprise: false,
    render: 'your_site_key',
    hl: 'en'
  });

  useHead({
    script: [
      {
        src: scriptSrc,
        async: true,
        defer: true
      }
    ]
  });

  nuxtApp.vueApp.use(googleReCaptcha, {
    type: 'v3',
    siteKey: 'your_site_key'
  });
});
```

# generateGoogleReCaptchaHiddenBadgeStyles.mdx

Source: https://github.com/siberiacancode/google-recaptcha/blob/main/packages/docs/content/docs/vue/references/generateGoogleReCaptchaHiddenBadgeStyles.mdx

title: generateGoogleReCaptchaHiddenBadgeStyles
description: Utility function for generating CSS styles to hide the Google reCAPTCHA badge

```ts
const styles = generateGoogleReCaptchaHiddenBadgeStyles();
```

## Return

Returns a string containing CSS styles that hide the Google reCAPTCHA badge.

<Callout>
  This utility is useful when you want to hide the reCAPTCHA badge while still complying with
  Google's terms of service. Make sure to include a visible reCAPTCHA badge or a text notice about
  reCAPTCHA usage on your page.
</Callout>

---

# generateGoogleReCaptchaScriptSrc.mdx

Source: https://github.com/siberiacancode/google-recaptcha/blob/main/packages/docs/content/docs/vue/references/generateGoogleReCaptchaScriptSrc.mdx

title: generateGoogleReCaptchaScriptSrc
description: Utility function for generating Google reCAPTCHA script source URL

```ts
const scriptSrc = generateGoogleReCaptchaScriptSrc({
  host,
  isEnterprise,
  render,
  hl,
  badge
});
```

## Parameters

| Parameter      | Type                                        | Required | Default        | Description                                        |
| -------------- | ------------------------------------------- | -------- | -------------- | -------------------------------------------------- |
| `host`         | `string`                                    | -        | `'google.com'` | The host for the script source URL                 |
| `isEnterprise` | `boolean`                                   | -        | `false`        | Whether to use the enterprise version of reCAPTCHA |
| `render`       | `string`                                    | Yes      | -              | The render parameter for the script source URL     |
| `hl`           | `string`                                    | -        | -              | The language code for the reCAPTCHA widget         |
| `badge`        | `'bottomright' \| 'bottomleft' \| 'inline'` | -        | -              | The position of the reCAPTCHA badge                |

## Return

Returns a string containing the complete URL for the Google reCAPTCHA script.

---

## Props

| `badge`    | `'bottomright' \| 'bottomleft' \| 'inline'` | -        | -       | Position of the reCAPTCHA badge           |
| `theme`    | `'light' \| 'dark'`                         | -        | -       | Theme of the reCAPTCHA badge              |
| `language` | `string`                                    | -        | -       | Language code for the reCAPTCHA badge     |

## Events

| Event          | Payload  | Description                                   |
| -------------- | -------- | --------------------------------------------- |
| `change`       | `string` | Emitted when the user completes the challenge |
| `error`        | -        | Emitted when an error occurs                  |
| `expired`      | -        | Emitted when the challenge expires            |
| `update:token` | `string` | Emitted when the token is updated             |
